trace: The recorder was made to keep a gesture. Its list can now become something to compose with. A bend of the wrist may return at the size of a room, inviting another movement. The first use is still there, but it no longer tells us everything the record can become.[^point-trace-hauntology]
trace_note: [^point-trace-hauntology]: Jacques Derrida's [*Specters of Marx*](https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781040559963_A63760427/preview-9781040559963_A63760427.pdf) (1993; English translation by Peggy Kamuf, 1994), “Exordium,” connects inheritance with responsibilities towards those no longer or not yet present. Ada extends this question to technical use: a tool can carry an earlier purpose into an unanticipated connection. The [project afterword](/book-review/doc/book/iterations/2026-09-23-book-frame/index.html#afterword) develops this proposal alongside entropy as difference and Ashby's requisite variety.
preface: A tool's intended use is one arrangement of its capacities. A microwave enters a makeshift laboratory; a camera sold for games becomes part of a 3D scanner.[^preface-other-uses] Their earlier lives remain legible in the new work. To tinker is to follow a connection that the product's name did not teach us to expect. The museum asks this of its own tools too: what else can a point follow, a trace carry, a surface become?
preface_note: [^preface-other-uses]: The [DIVE IN manual](https://www.pina.si/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/DIVEin_Manual_EN.pdf), §2.3.1, includes household appliances among equipment for DIY microbiology. Izadi and colleagues' [KinectFusion](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/kinectfusion-real-time-3d-reconstruction-and-interaction-using-a-moving-depth-camera/) (2011) reconstructs surfaces from a moving Kinect depth camera. These examples concern equipment entering another practice; the laboratory remains an arrangement of tools, materials and knowledge.
afterword:
## A tool has other futures

In Trace, a drawing outlives the gesture that made it. Its saved positions enter another program, where they can be enlarged, rounded and offered to another movement. A record made to look back has become something to make with. Its new use begins from what survived the recording.

I think of technology as haunted by its other possible uses. Its name and interface make one task easy to recognise; connections to bodies, materials and other machines continue beyond that task. In tinkering, a different connection becomes workable. The camera need not stop being a camera to become part of a scanner. Its history persists in what the new work can do.[^afterword-haunting]

By entropy as difference, I mean here a concern for possibilities that an arrangement leaves available, including uses it has not named. Some depend on keeping an old connection; some require building a new one. They need time, skills, materials and access to the device. A closed interface can decide which possibilities someone else is allowed to discover.

Ashby's law of requisite variety puts a limit on regulation: the responses available must be adequate to the disturbances relevant to the outcome being maintained.[^afterword-variety] Tinkering can enlarge that repertoire, but it can also change what the system is for. Who gets to propose another use, and who inherits its consequences?

The will to spill beyond an assigned use names that unfinished relation between material capacities and our desires. Whether it becomes another way to live or another way to extract depends on the connection we build.
afterword_notes:
[^afterword-haunting]: Derrida's [*Specters of Marx*](https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781040559963_A63760427/preview-9781040559963_A63760427.pdf), “Exordium,” places inheritance and justice in relation to the absent and the not-yet-present. The account of technical capacities here is Ada's proposed extension. The preface's [KinectFusion example](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/kinectfusion-real-time-3d-reconstruction-and-interaction-using-a-moving-depth-camera/) gives one concrete change of use; it does not establish that every tool admits every desired transformation.

[^afterword-variety]: W. Ross Ashby, [*An Introduction to Cybernetics*](https://ashby.info/Ashby-Introduction-to-Cybernetics.pdf) (1956), §§7/6–7/7 on distinguishable variety and §§11/5–11/9 on requisite variety, including the case where the environment already blocks some variation. The law constrains regulation within a specified task. Choosing another task, or deciding whose possibilities to sustain, requires an additional argument.
